definitions.explanation: A humble (kenjougo) expression meaning to listen. Used to show respect when referring to one's own act of listening to someone of higher status, such as a superior's speech or a teacher's lecture.

examples.japanese: ご{講演|こうえん}を{拝聴|はいちょう}しました。
examples.english: I had the honor of listening to your lecture.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}のお{話|はなし}を{拝聴|はいちょう}して、{大変|たいへん}{勉強|べんきょう}になりました。
examples.english: I learned a great deal from listening to your talk, sensei.

examples.japanese: {貴重|きちょう}なご{意見|いけん}を{拝聴|はいちょう}できる{機会|きかい}をいただき、{誠|まこと}にありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you very much for the opportunity to hear your valuable opinions.

notes:
USAGE:
{拝聴|はいちょう} is a humble ({謙譲語|けんじょうご}) form of {聞|き}く (to listen). It lowers the speaker's position relative to the person being listened to. Used in formal speeches, business settings, and polite correspondence.

The {拝|はい} prefix indicates humble respect and appears in other humble verbs: {拝見|はいけん} (to see, humble), {拝読|はいどく} (to read, humble), {拝借|はいしゃく} (to borrow, humble).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ご{講演|こうえん}を{拝聴|はいちょう}する (to listen to a lecture)
- お{話|はなし}を{拝聴|はいちょう}する (to listen to someone's talk)
- ご{意見|いけん}を{拝聴|はいちょう}する (to hear someone's opinion)
